findings.title: Missing GL Context Initialization Leads to UAF
findings.message: When rendering without presenting (present=false), the code skips calling mCompositor->BeginFrame(), which is responsible for calling MakeCurrent() to initialize the GL context. This causes wr_renderer_update() and wr_renderer_render() to execute OpenGL operations without a valid GL context being current. On systems with NVIDIA drivers, this can lead to the driver accessing freed memory or incorrect GL state, resulting in a use-after-free crash. The crash signature shows the issue occurs in libgdk-3.so.0 gdk_x11_app_launch_context_get_type, triggered during WebRender operations involving NVIDIA EGL libraries.

related_locations.description: wr_renderer_update is called after this block without ensuring GL context is current when present=false

findings.suggestion: When present=false, the code should still call mCompositor->MakeCurrent() to ensure the GL context is properly initialized before any WebRender operations. Add an else branch to handle the case when present is false to ensure GL context is current.

ground_truth.root_cause: The bug was introduced in Bug 1961115 which added a 'present' flag to skip compositor work when rendering offscreen content. The original code always called mCompositor->BeginFrame() which internally calls MakeCurrent() to establish the GL context. After the change, when present=false, neither BeginFrame() nor MakeCurrent() was called, leaving the GL context in an undefined state. Subsequent calls to wr_renderer_update() and wr_renderer_render() then operate without a valid GL context, causing NVIDIA EGL drivers to potentially access freed or invalid memory.

must_cover.reason: Contains the vulnerable control flow where present=false skips both BeginFrame() (line 198-227) and the fallback MakeCurrent() call (line 228-230 only executes when beginFrame=true but present=false). When present=false and beginFrame=true, execution reaches line 242 wr_renderer_update() without any GL context initialization, causing UAF when NVIDIA drivers access uninitialized GL state.

BeginFrame() is the normal path that calls MakeCurrent() (line 61) to initialize the GL context. Understanding that BeginFrame() performs this critical initialization is necessary to recognize that skipping it when present=false leaves the GL context uninitialized, enabling the UAF vulnerability.

Shows the correct pattern: Update() properly guards wr_renderer_update() call with MakeCurrent() check (line 164). This establishes that wr_renderer_update() requires a valid GL context. Comparing this with UpdateAndRender() reveals that UpdateAndRender() violates this invariant when present=false, making the bug detectable.
